claims.text: A thin Ni layer can be used as an adherent coating on a Cu matrix.
A thin Cr layer can be used as an adherent coating on a Cu matrix.
A Ni or Cr coating has excellent wear resistance.
A Ni or Cr coating provides surface-protection properties.
The proposed coating is a thin surface layer of Ni or Cr on a Cu matrix.
The proposed coating effect applies at room temperature and atmospheric pressure.
The relevant structural mediator is the interface between Cu and the Ni or Cr layer.
Ni or Cr atoms adhere at the interface and diffuse into the Cu matrix.
Interfacial adhesion and diffusion of Ni or Cr into Cu improve coating adhesion strength.
The coating increases adhesion strength by at least 20% relative to uncoated Cu.
The Ni or Cr coating should be less than 10 micrometres thick.
Coating adhesion depends on the surface roughness and cleanliness of the Cu matrix.
Interfacial reactions may occur between the coating and the Cu matrix.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 20% adhesion-strength increase, but the falsification rule tests only statistical significance. A statistically significant increase below 20% would fail the prediction without falsifying it under the stated rule.

The rule pairs 'not significantly higher' with p-value < 0.05; conventionally, p < 0.05 indicates statistical significance, whereas failure to establish a significant increase would generally correspond to p >= 0.05.
